items.title: Toshiko Akiyoshi interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 17, 1999
items.q: This is when I got very much into Bud Powell. And after that I think I would just play his record and I just learned how to play like that.

ctx.x: Did you start writing them down, or did they just become memorized immediately yourself?

At one time I used to write out everything. I remember I had quite a lot of standards a long time ago, like 78 records. But most of the time, much later I just played a number of them. This is when I got very much into Bud Powell. And after that I think I would just © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-

play his record and I just learned how to play like that. And by that time I had my little piano so mostly, most of the memorization was later on. First, early days, I used to copy it and put it on a tape.

items.title: Akiyoshi Toshiko — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I hadn‟t even heard Bud Powell... by that time there were many Bud Powell records and so on... I heard this “Body and Soul”... and that was Bud Powell. Since then, I tried to listen to him

ctx.x: Had you heard, uh, Charlie Parker or Dizzy Gillespie records by this time?

No, I hadn‟t. But they used to sing in “Oo-Pa-Pa-Da,” dah-da-da-dah, something like that, so on and so on. So, still, I hadn‟t even heard Bud Powell. That was still…. Then after this … I was asked to play in another band, called Gay Stars [chuckles], that‟s a big band. Then there was another one, this was called Six Lemons. It was Six Lemons … by this time, I was really copying things—by the time when I went to Six Lemons, there were jazz coffee shops sprouting in all places—and around those times, I heard Bud…
About what year is this now, maybe fift—.
